title: Pan-Seared Sirloin with Garlic Butter Potatoes
subtitle: a steakhouse-style dinner at home: crusty seared sirloin basted in garlic butter, with crispy roasted baby potatoes
imageAlt: Sliced pan-seared sirloin with garlic butter beside roasted baby potatoes on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and pat them very dry; they sear better.
Oven at 220°C (425°F) for the potatoes, which take longest.

steps.title: Roast the potatoes
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the potatoes with the oil, salt and garlic powder and roast cut side down on a rimmed baking sheet 30–35 minutes, until golden and tender.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Pat the steaks dry and season all over with the salt and pepper.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: With 15 minutes left on the potatoes, heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over high until it shimmers. Sear the steaks 4 minutes, without moving them, until deeply browned. Turn and cook 3 minutes.

steps.title: Baste
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter, smashed garlic and dried thyme and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks 1–2 minutes, until 63°C (145°F) for medium, Health Canada's minimum (or 57°C / 135°F if you prefer medium-rare).

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest the steaks on a board 8 minutes; the temperature rises a few degrees. Keep the garlic butter in the pan.

steps.title: Garlic butter potatoes
steps.text: Melt the 1 tbsp butter with the minced garlic in a small pan or the microwave 30 seconds, and toss with the hot potatoes.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Slice the steak across the grain and spoon the pan garlic butter over it. Serve with the potatoes.

fixIt.fix: The steak was wet or the pan wasn't hot enough. Dry it well and wait for the oil to shimmer.
Lower the heat to medium before adding the butter and garlic.
Slice thinly across the grain, and rest it the full 8 minutes.

saleTip: Sirloin is often half the price of striploin at No Frills; watch for 'family pack' sirloin on sale.
swap: Striploin steaks: same method, slightly more tender.
leftovers: Slice cold steak for sandwiches or steak and rice bowls; reheat gently or it overcooks.
doneness: Health Canada's minimum for whole cuts of beef is 63°C (145°F), medium. Medium-rare is 57°C (135°F), a personal choice below that minimum. Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested pan-seared, butter-basted steak methods (America's Test Kitchen, Canadian Living): dry, seasoned steaks seared in a hot pan, basted with garlic-thyme butter, rested before slicing.
gear: Large heavy skillet (cast iron is best)
prepAhead: Season the steaks up to 1 day ahead and leave them uncovered on a rack in the fridge for a drier, crustier sear.
reheat: Slices in a covered skillet over low with a spoon of butter, 2–3 minutes, until 74°C (165°F); potatoes at 200°C (400°F) 10 minutes.

basic.note: Salt-and-pepper steak and plain roasted potatoes.

stepNotes.5: Basic: skip; serve the potatoes as they are.

fancy.note: A quick creamy pan sauce and green beans.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: while the steaks rest, pour the broth into the skillet and boil 2 minutes, scraping up the brown bits. Add the cream and simmer 2 minutes until it coats a spoon.

addSteps.title: Green beans
addSteps.text: Boil the green beans 3–4 minutes until bright and just tender, drain and toss with a little of the pan sauce.

plating: Slices fanned on a warm plate.
Pan sauce spooned beside, not over the crust.

why.1-0: A thick steak gets a deep crust before the inside overcooks.
why.1-4: Basting with foaming butter browns the crust and carries the garlic flavour.
why.0-0: Baby potatoes roast creamy inside with no peeling.

funFact: Butter basting, 'arroser' in French, is how restaurant kitchens finish most steaks.

keeps.note: cooked steak dries out when frozen and reheated
